parsed.rationale: All four records are `type-alias-object` kinds with empty `fields_or_signature` lists, meaning each is a zero-field type alias (likely a typealias to a shared empty-struct message token). While they share the same structural shape (`shared_field_count: 1`, `differing_slots: null`), they encode four distinct domain events — application lifecycle (`ApplicationWillTerminateMessage` in `Core`), two separate playback-stall signals (`PlaybackStalledMessage` and `HLSPlaybackStalledMessage` in `Playback`), and a network-request event (`RequestSentMessage` in `MusicShareKit`). Collapsing them into a single shared type would conflate unrelated domain concepts and couple `MusicShareKit` and `Playback` to `Core` semantics they do not share. The structural coincidence is purely a consequence of the empty-message pattern, not evidence of a shared abstraction worth extracting.
